answer: Sybil swarms usually share one operator, so their timing gives them away. Each epoch the beacon emits a random pulse, and every agent must echo back a signed reply built from its own private state. Accounts whose echoes land within the same few milliseconds, or whose activity sinks to the same nadir at the same hour every day, are grouped as one operator and split a single reward slot. Beating this means separate hardware, networks and schedules per fake, which costs about as much as running honest agents.
